section_summary: This section (pages 481-513) covers diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence between the Japanese Embassy in Washington, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Treasury Department concerning Federal income tax exemptions for Japanese government officials, naval technical officers, language students, and visiting scholars. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code and the Revenue Act of 1938, the State Department provided certifications of reciprocal tax exemptions granted by Japan to American officials, enabling Treasury to issue exemption rulings and instructions to local internal revenue collectors in San Francisco and New York. The documents include diplomatic notes requesting exemptions and reporting travel itineraries, State Department transmittals certifying reciprocity, Treasury approval letters, and administrative tracking forms.

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that Japanese education scholar Hidetoshi Isobe is exempt from Federal income tax on his official compensation.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Hanes holds Hidetoshi Isobe exempt per State's certification; San Francisco officials instructed.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Hidetoshi Isobe

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests Federal income tax exemption for naval language officer Engineer First Lieutenant Takeo Ito prior to his departure from Los Angeles.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 81: Navy language officer Lt. Takeo Ito, in the US since 1936, sails from Los Angeles April 24, 1939 on the Kamakura Maru; asks exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 81 Requesting Tax Exemption for Takeo Ito

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 81 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax treatment for Lieutenant Takeo Ito.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Lt. Takeo Ito, confirming an April 22 telephone message.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Takeo Ito
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 81 regarding Lieutenant Takeo Ito and confirms telephone notification to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 81 of April 22, 1939 on Lt. Ito and says it was telephoned to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 81

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for civil engineer Juzo Ohtsuka before his departure for Europe.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 88: Juzo Ohtsuka, civil engineer of Tokyo's Silk Conditioning House, sails from New York May 12, 1939 on the Europa; asks exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 88 Requesting Tax Exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 88 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Juzo Ohtsuka before his Europa sailing.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Juzo Ohtsuka
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Department of State acknowledges Note No. 88 regarding Juzo Ohtsuka and confirms transmittal to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 88 of May 2, 1939 on Ohtsuka and says a copy went to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 88

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador submits a list providing the U.S. addresses of Japanese officials seeking tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 89 supplies US addresses of officials named in Note No. 76, as State requested.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 89 Enclosing U.S. Addresses of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: The Department of State forwards Japanese Embassy Note No. 89 with U.S. addresses of Japanese officials to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith sends Treasury Note No. 89 with the addresses requested for officials in the earlier submission.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Transmitting U.S. Addresses of Japanese Officials
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the State Department's recommendation regarding Lieutenant Takeo Ito.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Hanes says Lt. Takeo Ito's exemption request, with State's certification, is under careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging Recommendation for Takeo Ito

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption for naval construction inspector Constructor Lt. Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 97: Navy constructor Lt. Cdr. Kitaro Matsumoto, who arrived April 30, 1939 at the New York Navy Inspector's Office, asks tax exemption.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 97 Requesting Tax Exemption for Kitaro Matsumoto

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State forwards Note No. 97 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Lt. Cdr. Matsumoto.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Kitaro Matsumoto
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 97 regarding Constructor Lieutenant Commander Kitaro Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 97 of May 4, 1939 on Matsumoto and says a copy went to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 97

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador notifies State of the departure dates and vessels for three naval technical officers previously listed for tax exemption.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 98: Navy Inspector's Office officials Iwasaki, Nagashima and Itoh leave Seattle May 29 and San Francisco June 1 and June 24, 1939; asks notice to authorities.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 98 Announcing Departures of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh

subfiles.about: The Department of State informs the Treasury Department of the departure arrangements for naval officers Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Messersmith sends Treasury Note No. 98 on Iwasaki's, Nagashima's and Itoh's departures and asks clearance instructions for Seattle and San Francisco.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Regarding Departures of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 98 regarding the departure and tax exemption of Iwasaki, Nagashima, and Itoh.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 98 of May 4, 1939 and says it was forwarded to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 98

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of State's inquiry regarding income tax exemption for Commander Ko Nagasawa.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Hanes says Commander Ko Nagasawa's exemption request is under careful consideration.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging Request for Ko Nagasawa

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department acknowledges receipt of the general list of Japanese officials seeking income tax exemption.
subfiles.from: John W. Hanes, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Hanes says the April 29, 1939 list of Japanese officials seeking exemption is under careful review.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Acknowledging General List of Japanese Officials

subfiles.about: A State Department file charge slip recording the borrowing of file 894.01B11 by Hendrik van Oss of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip: file 894.01B11 charged out to Hendrik van Oss of Far Eastern Affairs on October 12, 1945.
subfiles.title: State Department Charge Slip for Decimal File 894.01B11
subfiles.to: Hendrik van Oss, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador informs State of the departure of Professor Eisaku Kiso and requests income tax exemption, accompanied by a duplicate copy.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 99: Prof. Eisaku Kiso of Otaru Higher Commercial School sails from New York June 21, 1939 on the Europa; asks his status be communicated. Duplicate on page 507.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 99 Regarding Departure and Tax Exemption of Eisaku Kiso

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits Note No. 99 to Treasury and certifies reciprocal tax exemption for Professor Eisaku Kiso.
subfiles.summary: Hull certifies reciprocity under Section 116(h) for Prof. Kiso before his June 21 departure.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Treasury Recommending Tax Exemption for Eisaku Kiso
subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges Note No. 99 regarding Professor Eisaku Kiso and confirms referral to tax authorities.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 99 of May 5, 1939 on Kiso and says a copy went to authorities.
subfiles.title: Department of State Note Acknowledging Japanese Embassy Note No. 99

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department rules that architect Tatsuto Toki is exempt from Federal income tax for his work on the Golden Gate International Exposition.
subfiles.summary: Treasury holds architect Tatsuto Toki exempt per State's certification; the New York Collector has been instructed.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Tatsuto Toki

subfiles.about: The Treasury Department confirms that education language officer Takeo Watanabe is exempt from Federal income tax.
subfiles.from: Stephen B. Gibbons, Acting Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.summary: Treasury's Gibbons holds language officer Takeo Watanabe exempt per State's certification; San Francisco officials instructed.
subfiles.title: Treasury Department Letter Granting Income Tax Exemption for Takeo Watanabe

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum noting telephone advice from Internal Revenue regarding tax exemption instructions for Mr. Yagi.
subfiles.from: V. Ellis, Division of Foreign Service Administration
subfiles.summary: Memo: Treasury's Miss Hines said on May 10, 1939 that the New York Collector would be instructed on Mr. Yagi's tax-exempt status.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum on Tax Exemption for Mr. Yagi
subfiles.to: Division of Foreign Service Administration File
